title: Neuron
body:
[[Binary Operations]]

---

The whole unit, and it is smaller than the name suggests:

$$
y = \sigma\!\left(\sum_{i} w_i x_i + b\right) = \sigma(\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{x} + b)
$$

Three parts, no more: a [[Dot Product]] of the inputs against the [[Weights]], a [[Bias Term]]
$b$ added on, and an [[Activation Function]] $\sigma$ applied to the result. That is a neuron.
Everything else in [[MACHINE LEARNING]] is arranging a great many of these and choosing the
numbers in them.

Read the two halves separately, because they do different jobs:

| Half | What it is | Fixed or learned |
|---|---|---|
| $\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{x} + b$ | an affine function, a weighted vote with a threshold | **learned** |
| $\sigma(\cdot)$ | a fixed squashing curve | **chosen**, never learned |

The linear half is where all the capacity lives; the [[Activation Function]] contributes no
parameters at all. But drop the activation and a stack of neurons collapses to a single linear
map, which is the argument in [[Non-Linear]] and the reason depth is worth anything.

## The bias is not optional

Without $b$ the decision boundary $\mathbf{w} \cdot \mathbf{x} = 0$ is forced through the origin.
The bias is what lets it sit anywhere, which is why Evan's [[Bias Term]] note says you need one at
every unit. It is the intercept of a line, with a different name.

## What one neuron can and cannot decide

With a step activation, a single neuron is a linear separator: it draws one hyperplane and answers
which side you are on. That is enough for the [[Binary Operations]] `AND` and `OR`, and famously
not enough for `XOR`, which is not linearly separable. [[Perceptron]] owns that argument and the
history attached to it; [[Multilayer Perceptron]] is the fix.

## The biological analogy, and where it stops

The name comes from a real cell: dendrites collect signals, the cell body sums them, and the axon
fires if the sum clears a threshold. The sum-and-threshold structure genuinely carried over. Almost
nothing else did. Real neurons spike in time rather than emitting a real number, they do not run
[[Back Propagation]], and the [[Weights]] here are just numbers in a [[Matrix]]. Treat the word as
a label for the formula above, not as a claim about brains.

## Related

- [[Perceptron]], [[Multilayer Perceptron]], [[Neural Network]]: what they get built into
- [[Forward Pass]]: an entire layer of these at once, as one [[Matrix Multiplication]]
